---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(tidyverse)
library(moments)
```

## 1. Carga y limpieza
```{r}
df <- read_csv("devops_metrics_clean.csv")
glimpse(df)
```

## 2. Descriptiva univariada
```{r}
describir <- function(x) tibble(
  media = mean(x, na.rm=TRUE), mediana = median(x, na.rm=TRUE),
  desv_est = sd(x, na.rm=TRUE), asimetria = skewness(x, na.rm=TRUE),
  curtosis = kurtosis(x, na.rm=TRUE))
describir(df$build_time_min)
```

## 3. Frecuencias (Sturges)
```{r}
k <- ceiling(1 + 3.322*log10(nrow(df)))
df %>% mutate(clase=cut(build_time_min,k)) %>% count(clase)
```

## 4. Analisis por grupos
```{r}
df %>% group_by(priority) %>%
  summarise(bugs=mean(num_bugs), fallos=mean(deploy_status=="failed"))
```

## 5. Relaciones bivariadas
```{r}
cor(df %>% select(commit_size_loc, num_bugs), use="complete.obs")
```

## 6. Visualizacion
```{r}
ggplot(df, aes(build_time_min)) + geom_histogram(bins=14, fill="steelblue")
```

## 7. Conclusiones
- A mayor prioridad, mas bugs y mas fallos.
- Los commits grandes se asocian a mas bugs (correlacion 0.42).
- Correlacion no implica causalidad.
